claim: Huntington's disease (HD) is initially characterized by an inability to suppress unwanted movements.
source: Huntington's disease (HD) is initially characterized by an inability to suppress unwanted movements, a deficit attributable to impaired synaptic activation of striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs).
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract describing a clinical characteristic of HD.

claim: The inability to suppress unwanted movements in HD is attributable to impaired synaptic activation of striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs).
source: Huntington's disease (HD) is initially characterized by an inability to suppress unwanted movements, a deficit attributable to impaired synaptic activation of striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs).
evidence: This is a mechanistic claim stated in the abstract.

claim: Distal dendrites of iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice were hypoexcitable.
source: Distal dendrites of iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice were hypoexcitable, a change that was attributable to increased association of dendritic Kv4 potassium channels with auxiliary KChIP subunits.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The hypoexcitability of distal dendrites of iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice was attributable to increased association of dendritic Kv4 potassium channels with auxiliary KChIP subunits.
source: Distal dendrites of iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice were hypoexcitable, a change that was attributable to increased association of dendritic Kv4 potassium channels with auxiliary KChIP subunits.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: The association of Kv4 channels with KChIP subunits was negatively modulated by TrkB receptor signaling.
source: This association was negatively modulated by TrkB receptor signaling.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by knocking-down expression of Kv4 channels.
source: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by knocking-down expression of Kv4 channels, by disrupting KChIP binding, by restoring TrkB receptor signaling or by lowering mutant-Htt (mHtt) levels with a zinc finger protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by disrupting KChIP binding.
source: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by knocking-down expression of Kv4 channels, by disrupting KChIP binding, by restoring TrkB receptor signaling or by lowering mutant-Htt (mHtt) levels with a zinc finger protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by restoring TrkB receptor signaling.
source: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by knocking-down expression of Kv4 channels, by disrupting KChIP binding, by restoring TrkB receptor signaling or by lowering mutant-Htt (mHtt) levels with a zinc finger protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by lowering mutant-Htt (mHtt) levels with a zinc finger protein.
source: Dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs was rescued by knocking-down expression of Kv4 channels, by disrupting KChIP binding, by restoring TrkB receptor signaling or by lowering mutant-Htt (mHtt) levels with a zinc finger protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: mHtt induces reversible alterations in the dendritic excitability of iSPNs that could contribute to the motor symptoms of HD.
source: Collectively, these studies demonstrate that mHtt induces reversible alterations in the dendritic excitability of iSPNs that could contribute to the motor symptoms of HD.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: HD is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded polyglutamine repeat in the huntingtin gene.
source: HD is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expanded polyglutamine repeat in the huntingtin gene (Zuccato et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about HD supported by a citation.

claim: At the outset of motor symptoms, HD patients have uncontrolled, choreic 'dance-like' movements.
source: At the outset of motor symptoms, HD patients have uncontrolled, choreic 'dance-like' movements.
evidence: This is a clinical observation about HD symptoms.

claim: HD symptoms are accompanied by down-regulation of phenotypic markers in striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs).
source: These symptoms are accompanied by down-regulation of phenotypic markers in striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs), which has led to the hypothesis that the hyperkinetic symptoms are due to a loss in indirect pathway function (Albin et al., 1992).
evidence: This is a statement about HD pathology supported by a citation.

claim: The hyperkinetic symptoms of HD are hypothesized to be due to a loss in indirect pathway function.
source: These symptoms are accompanied by down-regulation of phenotypic markers in striatal indirect pathway spiny projection neurons (iSPNs), which has led to the hypothesis that the hyperkinetic symptoms are due to a loss in indirect pathway function (Albin et al., 1992).
evidence: This is a hypothesis cited from the literature.

claim: Mutant Htt (mHtt) induces deficits in the synthesis, transport and release of brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).
source: Mutant Htt (mHtt) induces deficits in the synthesis, transport and release of brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) (Zuccato et al., 2010), as well as deficits in postsynaptic BDNF signaling through TrkB receptors (TrkBRs) (Ginés et al., 2010; Plotkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about mHtt effects supported by citations.

claim: mHtt induces deficits in postsynaptic BDNF signaling through TrkB receptors (TrkBRs).
source: Mutant Htt (mHtt) induces deficits in the synthesis, transport and release of brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) (Zuccato et al., 2010), as well as deficits in postsynaptic BDNF signaling through TrkB receptors (TrkBRs) (Ginés et al., 2010; Plotkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about mHtt effects supported by citations.

claim: In mouse models of HD, the progressive loss of TrkBR signaling leads to the disruption of long-term potentiation (LTP) at iSPN corticostriatal glutamatergic synapses.
source: In mouse models of HD, the progressive loss of TrkBR signaling leads to the disruption of long-term potentiation (LTP) at iSPN corticostriatal glutamatergic synapses (Plotkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work supported by a citation.

claim: Corticostriatal glutamatergic synapses are the principal source of excitatory input to iSPNs.
source: As corticostriatal glutamatergic synapses are the principal source of excitatory input to iSPNs (Bolam et al., 2000), the hyperkinetic symptoms of early stage HD could be due, in part, to a deficit in the ability to appropriately activate iSPNs (Plotkin and Surmeier, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about striatal anatomy supported by a citation.

claim: The hyperkinetic symptoms of early stage HD could be due, in part, to a deficit in the ability to appropriately activate iSPNs.
source: As corticostriatal glutamatergic synapses are the principal source of excitatory input to iSPNs (Bolam et al., 2000), the hyperkinetic symptoms of early stage HD could be due, in part, to a deficit in the ability to appropriately activate iSPNs (Plotkin and Surmeier, 2015).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by a citation.

claim: Kv4 K+ channels are key determinants of iSPN dendritic excitability.
source: Kv4 K+ channels are key determinants of iSPN dendritic excitability; these channels dampen dendritic propagation of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs), as well as somatically generated back-propagating action potentials (bAPs) (Day et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about Kv4 channel function supported by a citation.

claim: Kv4 K+ channels dampen dendritic propagation of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs).
source: Kv4 K+ channels are key determinants of iSPN dendritic excitability; these channels dampen dendritic propagation of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs), as well as somatically generated back-propagating action potentials (bAPs) (Day et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about Kv4 channel function supported by a citation.

claim: Kv4 K+ channels dampen somatically generated back-propagating action potentials (bAPs).
source: Kv4 K+ channels are key determinants of iSPN dendritic excitability; these channels dampen dendritic propagation of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs), as well as somatically generated back-propagating action potentials (bAPs) (Day et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about Kv4 channel function supported by a citation.

claim: Extracellular signal-regulated protein kinases (ERKs) are potently activated by TrkBRs.
source: For example, extracellular signal-regulated protein kinases (ERKs), which are potently activated by TrkBRs, phosphorylate Kv4 K+ channels limiting their activation in response to membrane depolarization (Hu et al., 2006; Schrader et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement about ERK activation supported by citations.

claim: ERKs phosphorylate Kv4 K+ channels limiting their activation in response to membrane depolarization.
source: For example, extracellular signal-regulated protein kinases (ERKs), which are potently activated by TrkBRs, phosphorylate Kv4 K+ channels limiting their activation in response to membrane depolarization (Hu et al., 2006; Schrader et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement about ERK effects on Kv4 channels supported by citations.

claim: Ca2+ influx through Cav3 Ca2+ channels diminishes inactivation of Kv4 channels and increases their ability to blunt sub-threshold depolarizing events.
source: Kv4 K+ channels also are modulated by local Ca2+ signaling; Ca2+ influx through Cav3 Ca2+ channels has the opposite effect of TrkBR signaling, diminishing inactivation of Kv4 channels and increasing their ability to blunt sub-threshold depolarizing events (Anderson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about Cav3 channel effects on Kv4 channels supported by a citation.

claim: The modulation of Kv4 channels by Cav3 Ca2+ channels requires an auxiliary subunit referred to as a K+ channel interacting protein (KChIP).
source: This modulation requires an auxiliary subunit referred to as a K+ channel interacting protein (KChIP) (Anderson et al., 2010; Shibata et al., 2003; Vacher and Trimmer, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about KChIP requirement supported by citations.

claim: KChIPs are required for ERK phosphorylation to negatively modulate Kv4 channel gating.
source: Interestingly, although it is unclear why, KChIPs are also required for ERK phosphorylation to negatively modulate Kv4 channel gating (Schrader et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about KChIP function supported by a citation.

claim: KChIPs, Cav3 Ca2+ channels and TrkBRs richly invest the distal dendrites of SPNs.
source: All three of these elements – KChIPs, Cav3 Ca2+ channels and TrkBRs – richly invest the distal dendrites of SPNs (Carter and Sabatini, 2004; Lobo et al., 2010; Plotkin et al., 2011; Rhodes et al., 2004) raising the possibility that they bidirectional regulate Kv4 K+ channel gating, as described in other neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about protein localization supported by citations.

claim: The dendritic excitability of iSPNs in two genetic mouse models of HD (BACHD and Q175) was depressed at an age (~6 months old) when mice became symptomatic.
source: Indeed, the dendritic excitability of iSPNs in two genetic mouse models of HD (BACHD and Q175) was depressed at an age (~6 months old) when mice became symptomatic.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: The reduction in dendritic excitability in HD iSPNs could be traced to enhanced opening of Kv4 K+ channels arising from increased association of Kv4 channels with auxiliary KChIP subunits and Cav3 Ca2+ channels.
source: The reduction in dendritic excitability could be traced to enhanced opening of Kv4 K+ channels arising from increased association of Kv4 channels with auxiliary KChIP subunits and Cav3 Ca2+ channels.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: Pharmacological or genetic suppression of p75NTR signaling pathways restored the ability of TrkBR signaling to modulate Kv4 channels in HD iSPNs.
source: Pharmacological or genetic suppression of p75NTR signaling pathways restored the ability of TrkBR signaling to modulate Kv4 channels in HD iSPNs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: Striatal suppression of mHtt transcription with a zinc finger protein (ZFP) reversed the iSPN deficits in both dendritic excitability and synaptic plasticity.
source: Finally, striatal suppression of mHtt transcription with a zinc finger protein (ZFP) (Garriga-Canut et al., 2012) reversed the iSPN deficits in both dendritic excitability and synaptic plasticity pointing to a regionally-autonomous mechanism in the disease phenotype.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: The reversal of iSPN deficits by striatal ZFP expression points to a regionally-autonomous mechanism in the disease phenotype.
source: Finally, striatal suppression of mHtt transcription with a zinc finger protein (ZFP) (Garriga-Canut et al., 2012) reversed the iSPN deficits in both dendritic excitability and synaptic plasticity pointing to a regionally-autonomous mechanism in the disease phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ZFP experiment results.

claim: The BACHD mouse is a transgenic model of HD in which the full-length human mHtt has been inserted using a bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC).
source: The BACHD mouse is a transgenic model of HD in which the full-length human mHtt has been inserted using a bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC).
evidence: This is a description of the BACHD mouse model.

claim: BACHD mice display progressive motor and physiological deficits.
source: These mice display progressive motor and physiological deficits.
evidence: This is a statement about the BACHD mouse phenotype supported by citations in the text.

claim: At 2–3 months of age, the deficits in BACHD mice are very modest but become more discernible by 6 months of age.
source: At 2–3 months of age, the deficits are very modest but become more discernible by 6 months of age.
evidence: This is a statement about the temporal progression of deficits in BACHD mice.

claim: Q175 mice have an Htt gene with an expanded CAG locus (175–180 repeats).
source: To cross validate results in the BACHD model, Q175 ±mice having an Htt gene with an expanded CAG locus (175–180 repeats) were also examined; these mice also manifest a progressive motor and physiological phenotype that becomes apparent at 6 months of age (Heikkinen et al., 2012; Menalled et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a description of the Q175 mouse model.

claim: Q175 mice manifest a progressive motor and physiological phenotype that becomes apparent at 6 months of age.
source: To cross validate results in the BACHD model, Q175 ±mice having an Htt gene with an expanded CAG locus (175–180 repeats) were also examined; these mice also manifest a progressive motor and physiological phenotype that becomes apparent at 6 months of age (Heikkinen et al., 2012; Menalled et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the Q175 mouse phenotype supported by citations.

claim: Action potentials (APs) evoked in the soma of SPNs by brief current steps, back-propagate into SPN dendrites.
source: Previous work has shown that action potentials (APs) evoked in the soma of SPNs by brief current steps, back-propagate into SPN dendrites.
evidence: This is a statement about SPN physiology based on previous work.

claim: Back-propagating APs (bAPs) transiently open voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels, which elevates cytosolic Ca2+ concentration.
source: These back-propagating APs (bAPs) transiently open voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels, which elevates cytosolic Ca2+ concentration (Carter et al., 2007; Day et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about bAP effects supported by citations.

claim: The bAP-evoked Ca2+ transient can be used as a surrogate measure of dendritic excitability as SPN dendrites are too small to directly record from with a patch electrode.
source: The bAP-evoked Ca2+ transient can be used as a surrogate measure of dendritic excitability as SPN dendrites are too small to directly record from with a patch electrode.
evidence: This is a methodological justification based on technical limitations.

claim: In iSPNs from both BACHD and Q175 HD mice, the ratio of distal to proximal bAP-evoked Ca2+ transients were smaller than in age-matched, wild-type iSPNs.
source: In iSPNs from both BACHD and Q175 HD mice, the ratio of distal to proximal bAP-evoked Ca2+ transients were smaller than in age-matched, wild-type iSPNs
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: The dendritic index of iSPNs from 6 month old BACHD mice was significantly smaller than that from wild-type iSPNs indicating a relative reduction in distal dendritic excitability.
source: In iSPNs from 6 month old BACHD mice, the dendritic index of iSPNs was significantly smaller than that from wild-type iSPNs indicating a relative reduction in distal dendritic excitability (Figure 1c–e).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1c-e.

claim: There was no difference in the dendritic index of age-matched dSPNs from BACHD mice compared to wild-type.
source: In contrast, there was no difference in the dendritic index of age-matched dSPNs from BACHD mice (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1e.

claim: A qualitatively similar loss of distal dendritic excitability was found in iSPNs from 6 month old Q175 ±mice.
source: A qualitatively similar loss of distal dendritic excitability was found in iSPNs from 6 month old Q175 ±mice (Figure 1f–h).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1f-h.

claim: Q175 ±dSPNs did not differ significantly from their wild-type littermates in dendritic index.
source: As for BACHD dSPNs, Q175 ±dSPNs did not differ significantly from their wild-type littermates.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1h.

claim: There was no discernible change in the dendritic architecture of HD iSPNs at 6 months of age.
source: Previous work had shown that there was no discernible change in the dendritic architecture of HD iSPNs at this age (Indersmitten et al., 2015; Plotkin et al., 2014), so physiological factors that might account for the drop in dendritic index were explored.
evidence: This is a statement based on previous work supported by citations.

claim: Quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis of mRNAs in iSPNs separated by fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) didn't reveal any significant change in the expression of either of the two primary Cav3 channel pore-forming subunits (Cav3.2, Cav3.3).
source: However, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis of mRNAs in iSPNs separated by fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) didn't reveal any significant change in the expression of either of the two primary Cav3 channel pore-forming subunits (Cav3.2, Cav3.3) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The attenuation of bAP-evoked dendritic Ca2+ transients in HD iSPNs could be a consequence of increased opening of Kv4 K+ channels.
source: The attenuation of bAP-evoked dendritic Ca2+ transients in HD iSPNs could be a consequence of increased opening of these channels (Johnston et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results supported by a citation.

claim: Four weeks after AAV injection of Kv4.2 shRNA, Kv4.2 mRNA was significantly reduced in the striatum.
source: Four weeks after AAV injection, Kv4.2 mRNA was significantly reduced in the striatum (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: In infected iSPNs, the relationship between somatically injected current and the frequency of spiking in HD iSPNs was shifted in a way expected from Kv4 knockdown.
source: Moreover, in infected iSPNs (Figure 2a), the relationship between somatically injected current and the frequency of spiking in HD iSPNs was shifted in a way expected from Kv4 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c–d).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c-d.

claim: iSPN dendrites were more excitable after Kv4.2 knockdown as bAPs evoked a robust Ca2+ transient in both proximal and distal dendrites.
source: More importantly iSPN dendrites also were more excitable as bAPs evoked a robust Ca2+ transient in both proximal and distal dendrites (Figure 2b–c).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2b-c.

claim: The relative excitability of distal dendrites of HD iSPNs after Kv4.2 knockdown was significantly greater than that of wild-type iSPNs.
source: In fact, the relative excitability of distal dendrites of HD iSPNs after Kv4.2 knockdown was significantly greater than that of wild-type iSPNs, in agreement with previous studies implicating Kv4 K+ channels in the regulation of basal excitability of distal dendrites (Day et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2c.

claim: At proximal iSPN dendrites, increasing the 4-AP concentration roughly doubled the response to optogenetic activation of corticostriatal terminals.
source: At synapses on proximal iSPN dendrites, increasing the 4-AP concentration roughly doubled the response to optogenetic activation of corticostriatal terminals (Figure 2d, left).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2d.

claim: 2 mM 4-AP had little effect on EPSPs when they were in the 0.5–1 mV range at the soma.
source: It is worth noting that 2 mM 4-AP had little effect on EPSPs when they were in the 0.5–1 mV range at the soma (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that Kv4 channels were largely postsynaptic and required a significant depolarization to be activated.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Kv4 channels were largely postsynaptic and required a significant depolarization to be activated.
source: It is worth noting that 2 mM 4-AP had little effect on EPSPs when they were in the 0.5–1 mV range at the soma (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that Kv4 channels were largely postsynaptic and required a significant depolarization to be activated.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on the 4-AP data.

claim: The magnitude of the 4-AP induced enhancement of EPSPs was similar at proximal synapses on HD and wild-type iSPNs.
source: The magnitude of the 4-AP induced enhancement of EPSPs was similar at proximal synapses on HD and wild-type iSPNs (Figure 2d, right).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2d.

claim: The Kv4 index at proximal synapses was not different between wild-type and HD iSPNs.
source: As inferred from the previous observations, the Kv4 index at proximal synapses was not different between wild-type and HD iSPNs (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2e.

claim: At distal synapses, 2 mM 4-AP roughly doubled the amplitude of the evoked EPSP in wild-type iSPNs.
source: At distal synapses, 2 mM 4-AP also roughly doubled the amplitude of the evoked EPSP in wild-type iSPNs (as in proximal dendrites), but in HD iSPNs the Kv4 index was significantly larger (Figure 2f,g).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2f.

claim: In HD iSPNs the Kv4 index at distal synapses was significantly larger than in wild-type iSPNs.
source: At distal synapses, 2 mM 4-AP also roughly doubled the amplitude of the evoked EPSP in wild-type iSPNs (as in proximal dendrites), but in HD iSPNs the Kv4 index was significantly larger (Figure 2f,g).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2f,g.

claim: The difference in Kv4 index at distal synapses was consistent with the proposition that in HD iSPNs, distal dendrites were less excitable because Kv4 K+ channels were more robustly engaged by depolarization.
source: This difference was consistent with the proposition that in HD iSPNs, distal dendrites were less excitable because Kv4 K+ channels were more robustly engaged by depolarization.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Kv4 index data.

claim: Quantitative PCR analysis of iSPNs separated by FACS revealed that iSPNs expressed mRNAs for auxiliary KChIP subunits.
source: Quantitative PCR analysis of iSPNs separated by FACS revealed that, in addition to mRNAs for Kv4.1, Kv4.2, Kv4.3 subunits, iSPNs expressed mRNAs for auxiliary KChIP subunits (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: There were no significant differences in Kv4 or KChIP mRNA expression between iSPNs taken from wild-type and HD mice.
source: However, there were no significant differences in Kv4 or KChIP mRNA expression between iSPNs taken from wild-type and HD mice.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: mRNA for Kv4.2 subunits was much more abundant in iSPNs than mRNAs for either Kv4.1 or Kv4.3 subunits.
source: The qPCR results also make the point that mRNA for Kv4.2 subunits was much more abundant in iSPNs than mRNAs for either Kv4.1 or Kv4.3 subunits.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Analysis of Kv4.2 immunoreactivity failed to find any difference in the density of Kv4.2 IR in proximal and distal dendrites of wildtype and Q175 iSPNs.
source: This analysis failed to find any difference in the density of Kv4.2 IR in proximal and distal dendrites of wildtype and Q175 iSPNs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Dialysis with a sub-type independent KChIP antibody (pan-KChIP; 1:50) rescued dendritic excitability in HD iSPNs.
source: Dialysis with a sub-type independent KChIP antibody (pan-KChIP; 1:50) rescued dendritic excitability in HD iSPNs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Dialysis of the KChIP2 antibody rescued dendritic excitability in HD iSPNs, whether measured using a bAP protocol or synaptic stimulation.
source: Dialysis of the KChIP2 antibody also rescued dendritic excitability in HD iSPNs, whether measured using a bAP protocol or synaptic stimulation (Figure 3a–d).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3a-d.

claim: Kv4.2 and Cav3.2 subunits could be co-immunoprecipitated from striatal tissue.
source: Indeed, Kv4.2 and Cav3.2 subunits could be co-immunoprecipitated from striatal tissue (Figure 3g) suggesting that they form a similar complex in iSPNs.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3g.

claim: The association between Kv4.2 and Cav3.2 was specific to Cav3 channels, as Cav1.3 Ca2+ channels did not co-immunoprecipitate with Kv4.2 channels.
source: This association was specific to Cav3 channels, as Cav1.3 Ca2+ channels did not co-immunoprecipitate with Kv4.2 channels (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The preferential Cav3 channel inhibitor mibefradil (3 µM) blunted the Kv4 channel attenuation of distal, optogenetically evoked EPSPs in HD iSPNs.
source: Moreover, consistent with previous work (Anderson et al., 2010), the preferential Cav3 channel inhibitor mibefradil (3 µM) blunted the Kv4 channel attenuation of distal, optogenetically evoked EPSPs in HD iSPNs (Figure 3h,i).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3h,i.

claim: Both KChIP1 and KChIP2, but not KChIP3/4, were robustly pulled down with a Kv4.2 antibody from striatal homogenates.
source: Both KChIP1 and KChIP2, but not KChIP3/4, were robustly pulled down with a Kv4.2 antibody (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4a.

claim: A pan-KChIP antibody was able to pull down Kv4.2 protein.
source: As expected, the pan-KChIP antibody was able to pull down Kv4.2 protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Antibody to Kv1.2 was unable to pulldown KChIPs.
source: However, antibody to other potassium channel subunits such as Kv1.2 was unable to pulldown KChIPs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b), and non-immune IgG did not pull down either Kv4.2 (not shown) or Cav3.2 protein (Figure 3g), supporting the notion that Kv4.2-KChIP interaction was specific.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Non-immune IgG did not pull down Cav3.2 protein, supporting the notion that Kv4.2-KChIP interaction was specific.
source: However, antibody to other potassium channel subunits such as Kv1.2 was unable to pulldown KChIPs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b), and non-immune IgG did not pull down either Kv4.2 (not shown) or Cav3.2 protein (Figure 3g), supporting the notion that Kv4.2-KChIP interaction was specific.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3g.

claim: In striatum, KChIP2 expression is enriched in SPNs and KChIP1 is mostly found in cholinergic interneurons.
source: In striatum, KChIP2 expression is enriched in SPNs and KChIP1 is mostly found in cholinergic interneurons (Rhodes et al., 2004; Xiong et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement about KChIP expression patterns supported by citations.

claim: There was a decrease in phosphorylation of Kv4.2 subunits at Thr607 and Thr602 in HD striata.
source: Indeed, there was a decrease in phosphorylation of Kv4.2 subunits at Thr607 and Thr602 in HD striata (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4b.

claim: In wild-type striata, BDNF significantly decreased the association of Kv4.2 subunits with KChIP2.
source: In wild-type striata, BDNF significantly decreased the association of Kv4.2 subunits with KChIP2 (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4c.

claim: In HD striata, BDNF did not significantly alter the association of Kv4.2 with KChIP2.
source: However, in HD striata, BDNF did not significantly alter the association of Kv4.2 with KChIP2 (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4d.

claim: There wasn't a detectable difference in the association of KChIP2 and Kv4.2 protein in unstimulated, wild-type and HD striata.
source: Somewhat surprisingly, there wasn't a detectable difference in the association of KChIP2 and Kv4.2 protein in unstimulated, wild-type and HD striata (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: In iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice, TrkBR signaling is impaired by aberrant p75NTR signaling through rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK).
source: In iSPNs from symptomatic HD mice, TrkBR signaling is impaired by aberrant p75NTR signaling through rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) (Plotkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement based on previous work supported by a citation.

claim: The selective ROCK inhibitor SR3850 (200 nM) rescued the ability of BDNF to dissociate KChIP2 from Kv4.2 channels in HD striata.
source: The selective ROCK inhibitor SR3850 (200 nM) (Chen et al., 2008) rescued the ability of BDNF to dissociate KChIP2 from Kv4.2 channels in HD striata (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 4e.

claim: TrkBR signaling normally leads to Kv4.2 subunit phosphorylation and the dissociation of KChIPs, which decreases Kv4 channel opening.
source: These results are consistent with the proposition that TrkBR signaling normally leads to Kv4.2 subunit phosphorylation and the dissociation of KChIPs, which decreases Kv4 channel opening (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the results stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 4f.

claim: In HD iSPNs, the impairment of TrkBR signaling appears to blunt the modulation of Kv4 channels increasing Kv4 channel opening and reducing dendritic excitability.
source: In HD iSPNs, the impairment of TrkBR signaling appears to blunt this modulation increasing Kv4 channel opening and reducing dendritic excitability.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the results.

claim: In wild-type iSPNs, BDNF enhanced both the proximal and distal bAP evoked Ca2+ transients.
source: In wild-type iSPNs, BDNF enhanced both the proximal and distal bAP evoked Ca2+ transients (Figure 5a,b) and significantly increased the dendritic index (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5a,b,c.

claim: In wild-type iSPNs, BDNF significantly increased the dendritic index.
source: In wild-type iSPNs, BDNF enhanced both the proximal and distal bAP evoked Ca2+ transients (Figure 5a,b) and significantly increased the dendritic index (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5c.

claim: In HD iSPNs, the ratio of distal to proximal dendritic excitability remained low in the presence of BDNF.
source: In HD iSPNs, the ratio of distal to proximal dendritic excitability remained low in the presence of BDNF (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5d.

claim: Knocking down PTEN using an AAV delivered shRNA effectively restored dendritic excitability to HD iSPNs.
source: First, phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) was knocked down using an AAV delivered shRNA (Stavarache et al., 2015); this effectively restored dendritic excitability to HD iSPNs (Figure 5d–f).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5d-f.

claim: Bath application of a TAT peptide pep5 (1 µM) targeting p75NTR restored the dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs.
source: Second, a TAT peptide pep5 (1 µM) targeting p75NTR was bath applied (Ilag et al., 1999; Yamashita and Tohyama, 2003); again, this intervention restored the dendritic excitability of HD iSPNs (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5f.

claim: In wild-type iSPNs, BDNF (50 nM) increased the amplitude of cortically evoked EPSPs.
source: As expected, in wild-type iSPNs, BDNF (50 nM) increased the amplitude of cortically evoked EPSPs (Figure 5g).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5g.

claim: Bath application of the selective ROCK inhibitor (SR3850, 200 nM) alone had no effect on the Kv4 index in wild-type iSPNs.
source: Bath application of the selective ROCK inhibitor (SR3850, 200 nM) alone had no effect on the Kv4 index (Figure 5h), in agreement with previous work suggesting little or no activation of this pathway in wild-type iSPNs (Plotkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5h.

claim: In HD iSPNs, the ROCK inhibitor enabled BDNF to boost EPSP amplitude and to decrease the relative engagement of Kv4 channels.
source: In contrast, in HD iSPNs, the ROCK inhibitor enabled BDNF to boost EPSP amplitude and to decrease the relative engagement of Kv4 channels, as estimated by Kv4 index (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 5h.

claim: Kv4 K+ channels regulate the dendritic propagation of bAPs in many neurons, including SPNs.
source: Kv4 K+ channels regulate the dendritic propagation of bAPs, as well as the response to local, synaptic depolarization in many neurons, including SPNs (Day et al., 2008; Hoffman et al., 1997; Johnston et al., 2000).

claim: By modulating bAP amplitude, Kv4 K+ channels control opening of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and dendritic Ca2+ influx.
source: By modulating bAP amplitude, Kv4 K+ channels control opening of voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and dendritic Ca2+ influx making bAP-evoked alterations in dendritic Ca2+ concentration a suitable surrogate measure of Kv4 channel function (Carter and Sabatini, 2004; Day et al., 2008; Häusser et al., 2000; Johnston et al., 2003).

claim: The up-regulation in Kv4 K+ channel currents in HD iSPNs was not attributable to a change in the expression of Kv4 subunit genes in HD striata.

claim: The up-regulation in Kv4 K+ channel currents in HD iSPNs was attributable to their association with KChIPs.

claim: Auxiliary KChIP subunits can increase the opening of Kv4 channels in response to depolarization.
